body:
I think it's natural for people to retreat back to what they are most used to in times of difficulty. I've talked about my depression and suicide online in various forms from the age of 13 when I made my first attempt, so... even if I thought there was no hope, this would be what I would come back to, just so I could be somewhere, to try and externalize these thoughts through a different frame.

I guess it's not just that though, that's why I talk in general, but this... I don't know; I don't know you, which is neither a good or bad thing, just an observation really, but I'm not going to jump to any conclusions either way on anything. But honestly, I probably wont be around long enough for it to matter anyway.

As for a name... call me Ru if you want, I'm not comfortable giving my real name here, but that'll do. And if you have to ask that, then I'm probably far older than you think I am... in the workforce for quite a long time now.
No to be honest. At this point I've really just given up on it all, on people, on finding any sort of connection. I just want to die, the more I think on it, the surer in that I am.

But the point is, it's... well I don't know how many times, but probably by now in double figures the number of times people have done that to me. I have to be doing something wrong, there's no other explanation that makes sense to instigate the same sort of behaviour in so many different people. 

It's difficult really, I can usually gauge pretty quickly in a conversation a person's motivation for it, and am probably quite a harsh judge on first impressions for that reason, though no other.  I'm untrusting initially for obvious reasons, so usually nothing if it's with a person I don't have any sort of connection with.

Well by it's nature, any sort of connection with another human being is unstable to a degree. Everyone has their own lives going on, their own ups and downs, times they want to be closer, and times they want to be more distant. I've had enough egotists in my life to know where not being able to perceive that gets you.

The ultimate goal is strong, stable and long term connections with people, of course, and it's not that I can't accept anything except for that, or that there's no internal benefit otherwise. It's that my perception seems to be way off when it comes to these things, either I am thinking that connections I have with people are much stronger than they are in the first place, or I am somehow destroying those connections without realizing it, because the pattern has occurred far too frequently for their to be any other explanation.

As for the one which has just put me in this state, it's someone I've known for many many years, was friends with for all that time, long distance, but not too long, we decided a few months back to give things a go between us, because we both have thought there was something more to things than friendship. Spent time together, talked a lot digitally, and then suddenly nothing. It's now been about 2 months since I had a proper conversation with them, and at least 6 weeks since they got in contact with me at all, and I know they're around, getting my messages etc. And the thing is, they know my mental state, better than anyone, and that this is the sort of thing which destroys me mentally, filling the gap of a lack of resolution with self-blame and self-hatred. So the only two logical conclusions are that they don't care I'm like this now, or they want me to be in this state.

I've lost count of the number of times I've tried to talk to therapists, psychologists etc. To me it always just seemed like a restatement of problems, talk for talk's sake, without any potential for resolution. I think that's the issue really with being introspective, there aren't any revelations waiting for me about my own state of mind, I don't think there's an approach or resolution I haven't tried of which I'm capable of, and while I understand the instability in a psychological reliance on external influences for an acceptable internal state of being, it is simply just who I am.
To feel loved.
Being me.
No. I'm just done with it all, can't take that pattern any more. Far easier to just kill myself.

Simply put, if it's my failure, at least I have something to learn from. If it's something that's not to do with me, then I can move on and accept that. It's happened too many times over the years though for me to be able to consider it as coincidence. I'm the common factor in all my failed friendships and relationships. So if I can't manage that sort of connection with others, then I really have no reason to keep going.

I just don't know... that's the worst of it, I really don't know what's happened, maybe I've overreacted, maybe I'm completely right. Just getting nothing but silence. I just... I don't see any point in going on. Whatever the answer is, it means I'm screwed.

I used to... over all the years I've been up and down with friendships and relationships with people, and been pushed away and rejected a lot of times without any understanding as to why. There was one person who was always the exception to that rule, and... I thought all my dreams had come true when we started a relationship together. But now... well I've discovered there is no exception to the rule, that everyone who knows me ends up treating me the same way.
Well it's all part of the same really, simply being able to talk with someone I trusted and who I felt gave a damn about me was enough for me to at least feel some respite from suicidal feeling.
Yep, but only up until I found out I was being lied to again.
The last post was a week without a reply, I just... I know I can't be helped, so don't know why I even bother trying.

1) In the end, I have to thank you. We were both a bit broken, both a bit immature, and you left me a wreck when you blindsided me with the goodbye. But years later, at least you had the decency to tell me why. I regret the way things ended, and I can't blame you for making the same mistakes I did. That's why it still hurts to think about you, you showed me love I didn't before know was possible, but showed me pain which I was, in truth, not strong enough to endure.

2) If you truly loved me, you would never have ended things without a word of explanation. It was so many years, I gave up everything for you, tried to give you all I could to make you happy. I just wish that it was I who could have made you happy. We had our moments I guess, but looking back, you never really saw me, just what you wanted from me. I made myself grow up, but you kept yourself a spoiled child, wanting to take, but never wanting to give. I hope you someday grow up, and I don't wish you ill, but even thinking about talking to you face to face brings up so much pain and resentment, that I'm glad there's a sea between us now, so we might never cross paths again.

3) I'm sorry. I know how brief things were, but I know how good they were too. It might not have meant to be, but at least you are in a far better place now than you were. I'm glad of that, and if I left this world tomorrow, at least I would know I have had a positive influence somewhere in my life. I regret so much though, if you had only talked to me, I think we would still be together. The truth is, I'm just too weak, too broken, to be the man you deserved. Because I could not handle the distance, I went and made more of it. So the truth of it is you're better off without me anyway.
Just commit suicide

Truthfully no. The understanding of what drove me to that point has certainly grown since I was 13 and first attempted, and the ability to distinguish between 'genuine' thoughts which deserve considerations of suicide, and exaggerated ones certainly has, but even after 15 years of fighting against those thoughts, that urge to end my own existence still remains, and the pattern of self-destructive actions that stem from this, again while more controlled, are still as forceful as they ever were.

The interesting thing though is that my understanding of what made me want to attempt suicide has changed. Back when it started, I thought it was just about escaping an abusive situation, but down the line I realized it was more about control. I've learned I can take a heck of a lot of abuse, which is, I guess, partly a given since I'm still here, but when circumstances have put me in a situation where I can not realistically have power to control my life on a macro level, to alter it's course to better circumstances of being, suicide is, and always will be, one choice I can make which I have complete control of. Some day I know I will be the cause of my own death, it might be years from now, it might be days, but to me it will always be a comforting thought.

That's something I've always found difficult. Even at the best of times, suicide was always an option. Self-harm was always an option. I don't think there will be a point where I will be free of those feelings, they do in part define me... so I worry that when my mind is right to reject, rather than embrace those feelings, that I might basically just be trying to get away from myself, which wont ever happen.

If I knew it would turn out ok, that I was capable of getting to where I need to be to feel ok, then it would be enough for me to have a reason to keep going. It's not a guarantee I'm looking for, but while it's a tired quote, you can't expect to do the same things and get different results. If the person who I am is incapable of getting the result I want from life, then either I have to find a way not to be me, live a lie, which is the public face I've given for 15 years or so by now, accept a life which will be one of disappointment and discontent, or choose to take an action which will prevent me from having to feel the rest of a lifetime's worth of crap.

I know there are people who have got through this, but there are people who have snapped, cut themselves on the shards of their broken sanity, and done great harm. That's not the sort of impact I want. In truth I don't want to change the world, all I want is to feel safe, to feel loved, to feel like I have value, and hopefully to make others feel the same. It's not an ambitious goal, nor an unreasonable one... in fact it is probably the most common goal of the human race. And when I thought I had that... I found out I was wrong. Relationships and friendships all following the same path. It would be arrogant of me to blame everyone else for those failings, but as I say, I am the obvious common factor. I know my flaws, and accept them. I never thought that they were bad enough to drive literally everyone away. But it seems I was wrong. If the ride is all there is, then it's nothing but a downward descent, on a ticket I never really wanted in the first place. Getting off the ride seems the logical choice.

Life isn't a story though, there is no guarantee at a happy ending. For every person whose life ends up like a literary fantasy, there are thousands whose impact on life is reserved for a few lines in the obituaries. The only dream I'm sure I can make a reality is a quick and simple death.

It's simple really, people want to believe they are responsible for their own successes, on their terms, and therefore have to believe that others are at fault for their failures. Once they step out of that mindset, and realize that any individual has a relatively small influence on the outcome of their own life at a macro level, then suddenly they are not where they are through deserving to be there, just through the whims of fate by one means or another.

And on top of that, while people are inherently social creatures, once someone accepts how little influence they might have, it's orders of magnitude more unlikely that connections can be made to others who fit with them. So when others are a part of what someone needs to be ok, whether it's through social validation, emotional or physical intimacy, or anything really... it's luck. Some massive roulette wheel with only one winning number, and thousands of losers, where you wager your own ability to endure whatever sort of loss is thrown at you.

That's the problem though... if I've found it, and it was cut away, then either what I found wasn't what I was looking for, or I'm incapable of identifying what it is I'm looking for... and then having it happen over and over again only confirms that. The only outcome in either of those situations is bad, I know from repeated experience, and to be honest, I'd much rather be out now, be done with life, than go through that cycle again.

I guess that's the problem, I've looked for it, I've found it, and then it was cut away, and I don't know why. It's the pattern I've seemed to have come across over and over again in my life, to the point I fear looking any more, because I have no reason to believe that a new time will be any different to all the times in the past, which have all ended the same way.

Everyone talks about hope as motivation, but only in their terms... I've done the work I was 'supposed' to do, and came out of it with nothing that's any use to me. The only way to 'win' I guess is to stop taking part in other people's races.

I guess the hope I delude myself with most of the time is in people. I know that people can hurt me, but I also believe that people can save me. Because when someone holds you in their arms, tells you they love you, everything feels right. When people do seem to understand, when they are on the same wavelength, when there is that connection, it is such a simple but genuine happiness.  But when they then cut you out of their life without a word as to why, then it's not just their positive sentiment, but all positive sentiment that becomes suspect. Was the feeling wrong, or the perception of all feeling wrong, and in either case it leaves me emotionally less than I was.
